fields.Frequency: ~2,000–3,000 claims/month across 200 stores (one register with W1630; ~10–15 per store/month)
fields.Trigger: Customer brings defective product with proof of purchase to store

Controls: - CTL-389 (ensure controlled execution — Warranty Claim Processing & Resolution (PA-53.2).)
- operational: Store Manager sign-off on borderline claims
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fraudulent-claim risk**: a customer claims warranty on a non-warranty item or a non-purchased item; mitigated by the serial-number match and the purchase verification (CTL-37)

- **Resolution-delay-dissatisfaction risk**: the customer expects immediate resolution but the claim requires vendor/service-center involvement (7–14 days); mitigated by the clear timeline-setting and the loaner-option for critical items
System Touchpoints: - CRM warranty (links to VS-13 / W17, VS-53 / W2118) — the warranty verification and claim record
- POS/inventory (links to VS-08 / W5B, VS-05 / W92 inventory adjustment) — the inventory adjustment on replacement
- Vendor notification (links to VS-53 / W2128 vendor escalation) — the vendor-claim push
Time Estimate: ~25 min/claim × ~9,000/month = **~3,750 hours/month CSR** (distributed across store CSR teams).

steps.activity: CSR verifies warranty in CRM; inspects product; photographs defect; checks serial number match
System classifies claim: standard (auto-approve), borderline (route to Supervisor), out-of-warranty (offer paid repair)
CSR offers resolution: immediate replacement, store credit, service center repair, or DC/vendor replacement (7–14 days)
Customer selects resolution; system processes inventory adjustment, creates claim record, notifies vendor

fields.Participants: Customer, CSA, CS Supervisor, Receiving Clerk
fields.Trigger: Customer submits claim via web portal or mobile app

Automation Opportunity: - Claim auto-routed to CSA worklist; return-QR auto-generated on approval; pickup auto-scheduled
Controls: - CTL-389 (ensure controlled execution — Warranty Claim Processing & Resolution (PA-53.2).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Photo-insufficiency risk**: the customer's photos don't clearly show the defect, delaying the claim; mitigated by the photo-guide (what to photograph) and the CSA's request-for-more-info
- **Drop-off-friction risk**: the customer must physically bring the item to a store, which for bulky items is a burden; mitigated by the pickup-scheduling option for bulky items
System Touchpoints: - Online portal/app (links to VS-53 / W2124, VS-75 app, VS-10) — the claim-submission surface
- CRM (links to VS-13 / W17) — the claim record and return authorization
- Returns/receiving (links to VS-32 / W12, VS-04 / W3) — the item receipt at store
Time Estimate: ~15 min/claim (CSA) + ~7 min (customer) × ~2,500/month ≈ ~37,500 CSA + ~17,500 customer min ≈ **~915 hours/month CSA + customer time (≈ 625 CSA + ~290 customer)**.

steps.activity: Customer describes defect, uploads photos/video, selects resolution and preferred store for drop-off
CSA reviews within 24 hours; validates photos match coverage; approves or requests more info; generates return authorization QR code
Customer drops item at store (scans QR) or schedules pickup for bulky items; store receives and triggers resolution

fields.Trigger: Claim requires manufacturer involvement (high-value >PHP 10K, complex product)

Automation Opportunity: - Claim auto-flagged for vendor escalation; vendor-SLA auto-tracked with escalation; vendor-scorecard auto-fed
Controls: - CTL-389 (ensure controlled execution — Warranty Claim Processing & Resolution (PA-53.2).)
- operational: Category Manager sign-off on vendor-SLA breaches
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor-SLA-breach risk**: the vendor doesn't resolve within 14 days, leaving the customer waiting; mitigated by the SLA-tracking and the Category Manager escalation
- **Vendor-deny-unjustified risk**: the vendor denies a valid claim to avoid cost; mitigated by the evidence-package (photos, serial, purchase proof) and the escalation to Category Manager
System Touchpoints: - Vendor portal (links to VS-28 / W593, VS-67 / W2458 vendor scorecard) — the vendor-claim submission and tracking
- CRM (links to VS-13 / W17) — the claim record
- Vendor scorecard (links to VS-67 / W2126) — the vendor warranty-claim performance feed

steps.activity: System auto-flags for vendor involvement; Coordinator packages claim with photos, purchase proof, serial number
Coordinator submits via vendor portal or email; tracks acknowledgment within 48 hours; manages vendor resolution (approve/return/deny)
Coordinator tracks 14-day vendor SLA; escalates to Category Manager if breached; monthly vendor warranty scorecard

fields.Trigger: Claim requires repair at authorized service center

Automation Opportunity: - Service-center auto-assigned (nearest); work-order auto-generated; SLA auto-tracked; failure-mode auto-logged
Controls: - CTL-389 (ensure controlled execution — Warranty Claim Processing & Resolution (PA-53.2).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Repair-delay risk**: the 7–14 day turnaround extends (parts backorder), leaving the customer without the product; mitigated by the SLA-tracking and the loaner/replacement option for extended delays

- **Non-covered-discovery risk**: the service center discovers the repair isn't warranty-covered (customer-caused damage), requiring a customer-paid quote after the item is already in the shop; mitigated by the pre-diagnosis at claim initiation (W2126) catching obvious non-covered cases early
System Touchpoints: - Service-center work-order (links to VS-12 / W440 power-tool service, VS-09 / W138 service sale) — the repair coordination
- Inventory/transfer (links to VS-05 / W22 transfers) — the item transfer store→service-center→store
- Quality/failure-mode (links to VS-31 / W110 supplier quality) — the failure-mode data for quality analysis
Time Estimate: ~45 min/case (coordinator) + 7–14 day repair (service center) × ~3,500/month = **~2,600 hours/month Coordinator** (distributed).

steps.activity: System assigns to nearest authorized service center; generates work order; arranges item transfer from store
Service center diagnoses: warranty-covered repair → proceed; non-covered → quote customer; beyond repair → replacement authorized
Repair complete; item returned to store; customer notified for pickup; failure mode data logged for quality analysis

fields.Participants: CS Supervisor, CSR, DC, Receiving Clerk
fields.Trigger: Approved claim resolved via product replacement

Automation Opportunity: - Replacement availability auto-checked across sources; reservation auto-made; warranty auto-transferred on pickup
Controls: - CTL-389 (ensure controlled execution — Warranty Claim Processing & Resolution (PA-53.2).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Replacement-out-of-stock risk**: the replacement item is out of stock (especially for discontinued products), leaving the customer without resolution; mitigated by the substitute-option or the refund-fallback (W2131)

- **Warranty-transfer-failure risk**: the warranty registration isn't transferred to the replacement item, so the replacement has no warranty; mitigated by the atomic replacement-and-warranty-transfer transaction
System Touchpoints: - Inventory/ATP (links to VS-05 / W105 multi-channel allocation, VS-60 / W2290 reservation) — the replacement availability
- Claim system (links to VS-53 / W2126) — the claim closure
- Warranty transfer (links to VS-53 / W2118) — the warranty registration transfer to the replacement
Time Estimate: ~5 min/pickup (clerk) + availability-check automated × ~5,500/month = **~460 hours/month** distributed (CSR + Receiving + DC).

steps.activity: System checks replacement availability: in-store (immediate), nearby store (1–2 days), DC (3–5 days), vendor PO (7–21 days)
For in-stock: inventory reserved, customer picks up. For DC-sourced: included in next shipment, tracking SMS sent
Upon pickup: scans replacement against claim; closes claim; transfers warranty registration to replacement item

fields.Participants: CSR, Store Manager, Finance, CS Supervisor
fields.Trigger: Claim resolved via refund (product unrepairable or customer preference)

Automation Opportunity: - Refund-eligibility auto-determined; proration auto-calculated; refund auto-processed to original method
Controls: - CTL-389 (ensure controlled execution — Warranty Claim Processing & Resolution (PA-53.2).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Refund-to-wrong-method risk**: the refund goes to a different payment method than the original (fraud vector); mitigated by the refund-to-original-payment-only policy (CTL pattern)
- **Proration-dispute risk**: the customer disputes the prorated amount (expected full refund); mitigated by the clear proration-policy documented at warranty activation
System Touchpoints: - Refund (links to VS-16 / W101 customer refund, VS-17 / W9) — the refund processing
- Claim system (links to VS-53 / W2126) — the claim closure
- Finance (links to VS-17 / W9, W70 credit/debit note) — the refund-to-original-payment
Time Estimate: ~25 min/case × ~1,000/month = **~420 hours/month** CSR + Store Manager + Finance.

steps.activity: CSR verifies refund eligibility; determines amount: full refund (<30 days), prorated (based on remaining period), or store credit at 110%
Store Manager approves refunds >PHP 5,000; Finance processes via original payment method; system closes claim

fields.Participants: CSR, CS Director, VP Merchandising, Legal

Automation Opportunity: - Dispute auto-routed with SLA; trend auto-analyzed; systemic-issue auto-flagged
Controls: - CTL-389 (ensure controlled execution — Warranty Claim Processing & Resolution (PA-53.2).)
- operational: CS Director sign-off; Legal review on high-value disputes
Pain Points / Risks: - **DTI-escalation risk**: an unresolved dispute escalates to the DTI (consumer protection), creating a regulatory complaint (W2682); mitigated by the 5-business-day resolution SLA and the goodwill-gesture option

- **Systemic-issue-neglect risk**: disputes recur on the same issue (a vendor consistently denies valid claims) without systemic action; mitigated by the monthly trend review and the corrective action
System Touchpoints: - CRM dispute (links to VS-13 / W41 complaint, W469 DTI escalation) — the dispute record
- Warranty terms (links to VS-53 / W2122) — the terms under dispute
- Vendor dispute (links to VS-67 / W2128, CTL-48) — the vendor-side escalation

steps.activity: Customer escalates; CSR logs dispute with additional evidence; CS Director reviews documentation, warranty terms, claim history
Director decides within 5 business days: overturn, uphold (with goodwill gesture), or escalate to Category Manager for vendor dispute
Monthly: Director reviews dispute trends; identifies systemic issues by vendor, category; implements corrective action

Automation Opportunity: - Analytics auto-generated; rate-increase auto-flagged; vendor/store auto-flagged at threshold
Controls: - CTL-389 (ensure controlled execution — Warranty Claim Processing & Resolution (PA-53.2).)
- operational: Category Manager sign-off on quality alerts
Pain Points / Risks: - **Quality-issue-late-detection risk**: a defective-batch claim-rate spike isn't detected until month-end, allowing more defective units to sell; mitigated by the weekly operational metrics (not just monthly)

- **Vendor-scorecard-lag risk**: the vendor-claim performance feeds the scorecard monthly, but the vendor negotiation is quarterly, so a claim-rate spike isn't acted on for months; mitigated by the >5%-trigger immediate vendor review (not waiting for the quarterly cycle)
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113, VS-67 / W2458 vendor scorecard) — the claim analytics
- Quality (links to VS-31 / W110 supplier quality) — the quality-alert target
- CRM (links to VS-13 / W17, VS-53 / W2126) — the claim dataset

steps.activity: System generates analytics: claim volume by category/vendor/store, claim rate by SKU, resolution time, cost, top 20 claim SKUs, repeat claim rate
Analytics Manager identifies trends: rate increase >2x triggers quality alert; vendor >5% triggers vendor review; store >2x average triggers investigation
